title: PPF for Children: Contributions & Tax Benefits for Parents

faq.q: Can both parents open separate PPF accounts for the same child?
faq.a: No, only one PPF account can be opened for a minor child, and it must be operated by one parent or a legal guardian.

faq.q: What if contributions exceed ₹1.5 lakh in a minor's PPF account?
faq.a: Any amount contributed beyond ₹1.5 lakh in a financial year to a minor's PPF account will not earn interest and will be refunded to the contributor.

faq.q: When does a minor's PPF account become a major account?
faq.a: The account becomes a major account when the child turns 18. The individual then needs to apply to change the account status and will operate it themselves.

faq.q: Can NRIs open a PPF account for their children?
faq.a: No, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are not eligible to open new PPF accounts. However, if a resident Indian opens a PPF account and subsequently becomes an NRI, they can continue to hold the account until maturity but cannot extend it.

faq.q: Is interest from a minor's PPF account taxable?
faq.a: No, the interest earned on a PPF account, whether for a minor or an adult, is completely tax-exempt under Section 10(11) of the Income Tax Act.

faq.q: Can I withdraw money from my child's PPF account before maturity?
faq.a: Partial withdrawals are allowed from the 7th financial year for specific purposes like higher education or medical treatment, subject to certain limits.
